authors: H. F. Holmes, C. F. Baes Jr., R. E. Mesmer
title: Isopiestic studies of aqueous solutions at elevated temperatures I. KCl, CaCl2, and MgCl2
experimental_method: Isopiestic method in a titanium-cup pressure vessel on a copper block, NaCl as reference, molalities from weighed cups with buoyancy corrections, 382 to 474 K.
uncertainties_stated: Weighing uncertainty below 0.1 per cent; corrected dilute molalities uncertain by not more than 0.4 per cent; results consistent to better than 0.002 in the isopiestic ratio R; duplicates agree within 0.1 per cent except MgCl2 (constant 2.0 per cent difference, single sample reported) and KCl at three highest temperatures.
quality_remarks: MgCl2 duplicates differed by a constant 2.0 per cent so only one sample is listed; KCl duplicates at 413.8, 445.4, 474.0 K differ because solutions went to dryness in heat-up, only one sample is listed; authors flag serious disagreements with literature MgCl2 osmotic coefficients. Printed MgCl2 1.9053 at 382.0 K (row NaCl 2.7044) is out of sequence with its neighbour 1.6047, probably a misprint; kept as printed.

not_extracted_tables.reason: Pitzer parameters fitted by the authors

extraction_notes: Text layer was parsed by script and every row compared with the 250 dpi page images (rows read visually from both pages); only the OCR glitches listed were repaired. Sanity checks (script): within each row NaCl < KCl and MgCl2 < NaCl; molalities are in no strict monotone order because left and right blocks are stacked (each block descends in NaCl). Replicate-like pairs (e.g. 6.2134/6.2020) are separate equilibrium points. Temperature scale and pressure not stated.
